title: Right to disconnect
summary: Employees may refuse unreasonable out-of-hours contact: from 26 August 2024 at employers with 15 or more employees, and from 26 August 2025 at small businesses.

instruments.title: Fair Work Legislation Amendment (Closing Loopholes No. 2) Act 2024

commenced.what: Applies to employers with 15 or more employees

direction_rationale: A labour-market rule rather than a competition measure; it may raise coordination costs for some firms and improve worker wellbeing.
comparison: Small versus larger employers during the one-year lag
confounders: new definition of casual employment on the same day

verified.notes: Dates from the Fair Work Commission's implementation report.

review.notes: Drafted by AI-assisted desk research on 18 October 2026 (legislation gap scan, docs/legislation_gap_scan.md) from the sources cited. Not yet checked by a person: verify dates, industries and the direction hypothesis before use.

assessment.summary: Employees may refuse unreasonable contact outside working hours. A workplace right aimed at wellbeing; for firms it adds policies and some coordination costs.

marks.reason: Employers need policies and practices to manage out-of-hours contact and disputes.
